scope: Sixteen selected formula families from four private documents. Documentation only; not an exhaustive archive inventory or a teaching pack.
reviewStatus: Source mapping complete for this bounded set; independent linguistic review pending.

privateSources.JN01: Pattern comparison notes; full document text and table structure read.
privateSources.JN02: Separate conditional comparison draft; full document text and table structure read.
privateSources.JN03: Foundational pattern notes; full document text and table structure read.
privateSources.JN04: Short conjunction gloss list; full readable text read.

sourcePolicy: Private file identifiers, exact filenames, hashes and locators are kept in the owner's companion source register. No original documents, personal examples or copied third-party lessons are distributed here.

families.topic: Hearing: 聞こえる / 聞ける
families.attachment: 聞く → 聞ける → 聞けます; 聞こえる → 聞こえます is a separate lexical verb. Use Nが in the first authored examples.
families.meaning: Audible sound versus the ability or opportunity to listen in a stated situation.
families.limits: Do not derive 聞こえる as a second conjugation of 聞く. Do not equate every occurrence of English 'can hear' with one form; do not teach volitional control as an absolute rule.
families.examples: Write new audibility and listening-access contexts, including one negative example for each. Source examples need editing and are not answer keys.
families.marathi: A contrast explanation exists; rewrite as ऐकू येणे versus ऐकण्याची संधी/सोय असणे with context. Draft Marathi and English wording still needs review.
blockers: Revise the current ability lesson's overly broad 'one can' framing in the pilot PR.
Author and review readings, meanings and narrowly contextual answer keys.

families.topic: Seeing: 見える / 見られる
families.attachment: 見る → 見られる → 見られます; 見える → 見えます is a separate lexical verb.
families.meaning: Something is visible versus an opportunity or ability to see/watch.
families.limits: 見られる also has passive/honorific readings in other contexts. Use explicit opportunity contexts; colloquial 見れる is outside the first pilot.
families.examples: Author a view from a location and access to a showing. Do not copy the hearing examples accidentally repeated in the source's seeing section.
families.marathi: Comparison exists, but part of the draft repeats hearing material. Rebuild the pair with दिसणे and पाहण्याची संधी/सोय असणे.
blockers: Review polysemy and new example pairs after the hearing pilot.

families.topic: General potential and ことができる
families.attachment: Explicit verb class, dictionary form, potential form and polite form; dictionary form + ことができる.
families.meaning: Ability or possibility, distinguished from an event simply being completed or ready.
families.limits: Do not generate all verbs by a single stem rule. Separate lexical できる senses and verbs without an ordinary potential form.
families.examples: Existing swimming/coming examples are app coverage, not proof the private formulas were imported.
families.marathi: Partial explanatory notes; no complete reviewed class-by-class Marathi pack.
blockers: Resolve source category confusion and the scope of permission claims before expanding the general lesson.

families.topic: Experience: Vたことがある / ない
families.attachment: Past plain verb + ことがある / ことがない; record the chosen verb's actual past form.
families.limits: The source's count restriction needs correction; experience does not itself specify exactly one occurrence.
families.examples: Current app has prior-experience examples; new contrast tasks should distinguish experience from a single dated event.
families.marathi: Only partial notes in this source section; bundled Marathi example meanings do not supply a full formula explanation.
blockers: Check meaning/count wording and author examples before selecting an activity.

families.topic: Ease and difficulty: やすい / にくい
families.attachment: Verb ます stem + やすい / にくい; record adjective inflection and verb class explicitly.
families.meaning: An action is easy or difficult to perform in context.
families.limits: The source has formula headings with empty explanation/example cells. Do not treat headings as reviewed teaching content.
families.examples: New readable/easy-to-use contexts are needed; none is selected as an answer key.
families.marathi: No developed Marathi explanation in the mapped section.
blockers: Fill meaning, context, inflection and exceptions from an independent reference.

families.topic: Conditions and concession: と / ば / たら / なら / ても
families.attachment: Review verb, い-adjective, な-adjective and noun attachment separately. Never apply a generic 'ます stem + ending' algorithm.
families.meaning: Habitual result, hypothesis, temporal sequence, topic-based condition and concession are distinct lesson objectives.
families.limits: Conflicting columns and blanket restrictions in the drafts cannot become universal valid/invalid labels. ても must retain its concessive meaning.
families.examples: Machine-result, advice and future-sequence cases occur in the notes; all require context-specific re-authoring.
families.marathi: Sparse labels and partial comparisons; no complete five-way explanation.
blockers: Resolve contradictory restrictions and misplaced examples.
Split the five-way chart into small lessons after a fuller reference review.

families.topic: Completion and regret: てしまう / ちゃう / じゃう
families.attachment: Review contraction from the actual て/で form, then inflect the resulting form; do not use the conflicting dictionary-ending lists.
families.meaning: Completion and unwanted-result/regret uses, with casual contractions.
families.limits: Do not teach every completion as an accident. Malformed past contractions and mismatched verbs appear in the draft.
families.examples: Author ordinary completion and unintended-result pairs; source sentences are correction candidates.
families.marathi: No complete Marathi contrast pack in the mapped tables.
blockers: Validate conjugation, transitivity, register and tense before drafting exercises.

families.topic: Without doing: ずに / ないで
families.attachment: Review the negative-base connection and irregular する → せずに; the draft's general ます-stem rule is unsuitable.
families.meaning: One action happens without another action being performed.
families.limits: Do not automatically substitute in every negative て-form construction or generate all verbs from ます stems.
families.examples: The notes contrast doing an action before another with omitting it; author fresh examples after checking the forms.
families.marathi: Paired करून / न करता explanations exist.
blockers: Verify formation and the boundary with causal negative constructions.

families.attachment: Plain clause + nominalizer + the particle required by the following predicate.
families.meaning: Treat an action or event as a noun-like constituent; restrictions depend on the following expression.
families.limits: Reject the shortcut 'の only with perception, こと everywhere else'; some contexts allow both and fixed expressions constrain the choice.
families.examples: The file contains copied lesson text as well as notes. Write new examples rather than distributing that transcript.
families.marathi: Partial transliterated Marathi explanation; rewrite in reviewed natural Marathi.
blockers: Review overlap, fixed expressions and independent examples.

families.attachment: Actual verb て-form + いる; interpret the construction using the verb and context.
families.meaning: Ongoing activity, resulting state and habitual/current situation need separate contexts.
families.limits: Several source cells contain unrelated copied explanations; do not map all uses to English present continuous or Vた + います.
families.examples: Existing app has action/state examples. New tasks need explicit time or state cues.
families.marathi: No complete Marathi explanation set in these sections.
blockers: Reconcile column mismatches and remove placeholder meanings before reuse.

families.topic: Preparation and result: ておく / てある
families.attachment: Review verb て-form and the construction's participant/particle pattern separately; casual contractions are a later subtopic.
families.meaning: Doing something in preparation or leaving it so versus describing a resulting prepared state.
families.limits: Do not import the draft's equality chain as unrestricted interchangeability.
families.examples: New preparation/result context pairs needed; private examples are not selected.
families.marathi: No developed Marathi comparison in the mapped section.
blockers: Check transitivity, viewpoint, particles and register.

families.topic: Reason versus concession: から / ので / のに
families.attachment: Review clause attachment, including noun/な-adjective forms; distinguish concessive のに from purpose のに.
families.meaning: Reasons and an outcome contrary to expectation are separate senses.
families.limits: The existing because lesson is only partial coverage. Avoid an absolute rude/polite rule based solely on から versus ので.
families.examples: The notes have contrasts; replace personal dialogue with fresh contextual pairs.
families.marathi: Useful reason/concession comparisons exist, with some oversimplified register labels.
blockers: Review attachment, register and separate senses before import.

families.topic: Desire and plans: たい / ほしい / つもり / 予定
families.attachment: Review ます stem + たい, noun + がほしい, verb + つもり, and verb/noun + 予定 as separate records.
families.meaning: A desired action/item, an intention and a schedule are distinct.
families.limits: Perspective, reported desire and opinion versus intention are mixed in parts of the draft; do not infer another person's inner state from a fixed formula alone.
families.examples: Current app covers たい and some future plans. New cases need fictional speakers and consistent viewpoint.
families.marathi: Partial explanations exist; some translations conflate viewpoint.
blockers: Resolve viewpoint, particle and meaning mismatches; replace personal examples.

families.topic: Comparison: より / ほう / ほど
families.attachment: Explicit compared items and quality; review adjective class and negative form in the ほど construction.
families.meaning: Relative degree and not reaching another item's degree, with comparison questions.
families.limits: Do not reverse the compared items, infer real-world rankings, or use an い-adjective ending for every predicate.
families.examples: Author fictional comparison data rather than reuse unsupported city/language rankings.
families.marathi: Limited explanatory labels, not a reviewed comparison lesson.
blockers: Complete meanings and resolve incomplete or mismatched comparison cells.

families.attachment: Separate です/ます, honorific and humble constructions; review lexical exceptions and participant roles.
families.meaning: Listener politeness and treatment of the person whose action is described are different dimensions.
families.limits: The app covers basic polite endings only. The source's gender and first/second-person shortcuts are not universal rules.
families.examples: Use fictional role-based conversations after specialist review.
families.marathi: No complete Marathi explanation set in these tables.
blockers: Review social context, special verbs, malformed examples and gender generalizations.

families.attachment: Standalone connector + clause; do not confuse it with a similar-looking attached grammar construction.
families.meaning: Topic change, related detail and unexpected result must be distinguished by conversational intention.
families.limits: Source ところで entries relate to the current pilot; the short list alone does not establish the ちなみに contrast or validate the pilot.
families.examples: Keep the existing authored activity. Expansion requires contextual examples and source checking.
families.marathi: Current pilot has draft Marathi; the short source list is mainly English glosses.
blockers: Do not duplicate the current activity or claim the conjunction archive is implemented.
